rejected_interpretation.description: The material-18 FieldCliffShader01 rim on terrain assemblies 30 and 35 was initially transferred as runtime material mode 27.
rejected_interpretation.reason: Neither assembly is the sign-side dirt ramp identified by the user. The referenced surface is material 19 on ground mesh 36, and its visible sweep is already authored through Color0 and Alpha_light. A cliff rim was therefore the wrong source signal.
rejected_interpretation.correction: Material mode 27 and its separate dirt-ramp render object were removed from every renderer backend and the game runtime.

source_ramp.source_surface_equation: surface = mask.rgb * Color0.rgb * textureSurface + Alpha_light * (1 - Color0.a)
observations: The complete dirt slope is material 19 on source mesh 36; it is not a material-18 cliff cap.
The high edge carries white Color0 with alpha 0.749019623, while the low edge carries warm dirt Color0 with alpha 0.800000012.
A brighter low control occurs at the ramp center. Source triangle interpolation creates a lateral highlight in addition to the high-to-low sweep.
Because Color0 alpha is below one, FieldGroundShader01 adds its authored Alpha_light. Ordinary generated dirt colors with alpha one disable this source effect.

The high-side flat continues from white alpha 0.749019623 at z=-900 cm to alpha 1.0 controls near z=-1000 cm. The light contribution therefore resolves across neighboring flat ground instead of stopping at the slope seam.
The low-side landing retains alpha 0.800000012 while its warm edge and brighter center controls resolve toward white by z=-800 cm.

implementation_contract.material_preservation: Every generated surface remains in the same continuous material-mode-4 FieldGroundShader01 draw. No new shader mode, rim equation, or specular approximation is used.
implementation_contract.normalized_transfer: Dirt ramps interpolate the exact source low-edge, low-center, and high Color0 controls over their normalized elevation and cross-ramp position. The lateral interpolation is linear, matching the source triangles.
implementation_contract.adjacent_flat_transition: A matching-height flat dirt tile directly touching a dirt ramp linearly interpolates from the exact shared ramp-edge Color0/alpha back to that flat tile's normal target-family Color0 across one tile. High and low ramp sides are resolved independently; a rare multi-ramp corner averages its boundary controls with smooth-union coverage.
implementation_contract.adjacent_lawn_transition: A matching-profile lawn edge donates its continuous world-space target-family Color0 to every touching dirt shape. Flat dirt blends from that shared value back to its normal dirt field, while a ramp blends back to the source sign-ramp Color0/Alpha_light field, over the recovered 30 cm ground ribbon. Both joins therefore avoid a straight tint delimiter.
implementation_contract.surface_isolation: Only directional dirt ramps and directly connected flat dirt neighbors receive the source ramp field. Unrelated flat dirt and lawn interiors retain their target-family Color0 fields; only a touching 30 cm dirt/lawn ribbon receives the neighboring lawn value.
implementation_contract.renderer_parity: The effect uses the already-qualified FieldGroundShader01 material-mode-4 path shared by OpenGL, D3D12, Vulkan direct, and Vulkan indirect.
implementation_contract.preview_parity: Standalone dirt-ramp prefabs and merged edited-scene ramps are generated by the same terrain surface builder.

claim_boundary: LGPE stores this ramp and its adjacent flats as continuous Route 1 ground geometry rather than reusable one-metre tiles. The Color0 controls, continuation into neighboring ground, and FieldGround equation are exact source evidence; fitting that field across the editor's cardinal ramp and one directly connected flat tile per side is the documented reconstruction.
